@@ -2,10 +2,69 @@
 
 **A flight recorder for AI coding agents.**
 
-`bbx` records what Claude Code does in your repository into an append-only, hash-chained log. When something breaks, it produces an incident report. It can tell you which lines were written by the agent, in which session, and from which prompt.
+`bbx` records what Claude Code does in your repository into an append-only, hash-chained log. Every prompt, tool call, file edit and command goes into `.blackbox/`. Later milestones turn that log into incident reports and line-level provenance ("which prompt wrote this line?").
 
-> Status: early development (Milestone 0). Nothing works yet beyond the skeleton.
+> Status: Milestone 1 of the v0.1 plan. Recording, `init` and `verify` work. `timeline`, `report`, `blame` and `investigate` come next.
 
+## Quick start
+
+```
+dotnet build -c Release
+cd your-project
+path/to/bbx init --local      # hooks point at this bbx binary (settings.local.json)
+# or, with bbx on PATH:
+bbx init                      # hooks go to .claude/settings.json, shared with the team
+```
+
+Then use Claude Code as usual. Check the log at any time:
+
+```
+bbx verify
+```
+
+## Commands
+
+| Command | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `bbx init [--local] [--private]` | Creates `.blackbox/` and merges hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json` with `--local`). Existing settings and hooks are kept; a `.bbx-backup` copy is written first. Running it twice changes nothing. |
+| `bbx init --uninstall` | Removes bbx hooks from both settings files. Leaves `.blackbox/` alone. |
+| `bbx hook <event>` | Called by Claude Code. Reads the hook payload from stdin and appends one record. Always exits 0, never prints. |
+| `bbx verify` | Recomputes every session's hash chain. Exit code 1 if a record was edited, deleted or reordered. |
+
+## What it records
+
+One JSONL file per session in `.blackbox/sessions/`. Each line has `seq`, `ts`, `event` (raw hook name), `kind` (`PromptSubmitted`, `FileModified`, `TestCompleted`, ...), `actor`, `prompt_seq` (the prompt that led to it), event `data`, and `prev`/`hash` for the chain.
+
+- File edits: repo-relative path, diff (capped at 16 KB), added/removed line counts, normalized hashes of added lines, SHA-256 of the file before and after. Never the full file.
+- Commands: the command, exit code, the last 1 KB of output. Test and build commands are recognized (`dotnet test`, `npm test`, `pytest`, `cargo build`, ...).
+- Prompts: full text by default; `record_prompts` can be `hash` or `off`.
+
+## Privacy
+
+Redaction runs before anything touches the disk: API keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, private keys, passwords in connection strings and `.env` lines, credentials in URLs, plus your home directory and user name. Files matching `ignore_paths` (`.env*`, `**/secrets/**`, `*.pem`, `*.pfx`, `appsettings.*.json` by default) are recorded as "changed" with no diff or hashes. Transcript and scratchpad paths from Claude Code are dropped.
+
+`.blackbox/` is committed by default so the team shares provenance. `bbx init --private` adds it to `.gitignore` instead. Redaction is pattern-based and can miss things; see [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md).
+
+## How it works
+
+```
+record[n].hash = SHA256( record[n].prev + "\n" + canonical_json(record[n] without hash) )
+record[n].prev = record[n-1].hash        (record[0].prev = "sha256:GENESIS")
+```
+
+The chain is **tamper-evident, not tamper-proof**. It catches edits, deletions and reordering inside a log. Someone with write access can still regenerate the whole chain from scratch. Anchoring the chain head in git commits is planned for v0.2.
+
+It also only sees what Claude Code passes to hooks. Commands you run in another terminal are not recorded.
+
+## Performance
+
+Each hook is a separate process, so start-up time matters. `bbx` is compiled with Native AOT. `scripts/bench-hook.ps1` measures it the way Claude Code calls it.
+
+| Build | Median per hook (Windows) |
+|---|---|
+| JIT (framework-dependent) | 128 ms |
+| Native AOT | measured in CI, see the `aot` job |
+

export PATH="$PATH:/c/Program Files/GitHub CLI" && git push -u origin milestone/1-recorder 2>&1 | tail -3 && gh pr create --base main --head milestone/1-recorder --title "Milestone 1: recording core (hook, init, verify)" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What

Milestone 1 of the v0.1 plan: the recorder works end to end.

- `bbx hook <event>` records Claude Code hook events into hash-chained JSONL under `.blackbox/sessions/`. Always exits 0, writes nothing to stdout/stderr, 2 s ceiling, errors go to `.blackbox/errors.log`.
- `bbx init` merges hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (`--local`: `settings.local.json` with the binary's absolute path), backs up first, idempotent; `--private`, `--uninstall`.
- `bbx verify` recomputes every chain and reports the first broken record (exit 1).
- Redaction before disk: tokens, keys, JWTs, private keys, passwords, `.env` lines, URL credentials, home directories and the user name. `ignore_paths`, `record_prompts`.
- Records: semantic `kind`, `actor`, `prompt_seq`, diff + added-line hashes + before/after file hashes for edits, exit code and output tail for commands, test/build recognition.
- Listens to `PostToolUseFailure` too (failed tool calls don't arrive as `PostToolUse`).

## Verification

- 133 tests (117 Core, 16 CLI). Core line coverage 95.3% (`tests/coverage.runsettings`).
- Fixtures are real hook payloads captured on Windows, scrubbed.
- Dogfooding: this repo has `bbx init --local` installed and the session that built it is being recorded; `bbx verify` passes.
- New CI job `aot` publishes with Native AOT on Linux, Windows and macOS (any AOT/trim warning fails it) and runs `scripts/bench-hook.ps1`.

## Not done here

- Local AOT measurement on the target Windows machine (needs a newer .NET 10 SDK and the C++ toolchain). JIT build: 128 ms median per hook.
- `.blackbox/` recordings are not committed yet; that is a separate decision.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

data.message:
Milestone 1 bitti ve PR açıldı: [sayinbrahim/agent-blackbox#1](https://github.com/sayinbrahim/agent-blackbox/pull/1). CI şu an çalışıyor; AOT hızı da oradan ölçülecek, sonucu henüz görmedim.

## Ne çalışıyor

- **`bbx hook <event>`:** Claude Code'un yedi event'ini zincirli JSONL dosyalarına yazıyor: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd. Her koşulda exit 0 ile çıkıyor, stdout'a da stderr'e de hiçbir şey yazmıyor. Hata olursa `errors.log`'a yazıyor; bir kaydın üst süresi 2 saniye.
- **`bbx init`:** mevcut ayarları ve hook'ları koruyarak birleştiriyor ve önce yedek alıyor. İki kez çalıştırınca hiçbir şey değişmiyor. `--local`, `--private` ve `--uninstall` bayrakları var.
- **`bbx verify`:** kaydın düzenlendiğini, silindiğini veya sırasının bozulduğunu yakalıyor. Örnek çıktı: "tampered at seq 2 (prev hash mismatch)". Zincir kırıksa exit 1 ile çıkıyor.
- **Redaction:** secret'lar diske yazılmadan önce maskeleniyor. Buna ek olarak ev dizinin ve kullanıcı adın da maskeleniyor. Bunu, `ls` çıktısında adın göründüğünü fark edince ekledim.
- **Testler:** 133 test geçiyor (Core'da 117, CLI'da 16). Core'un satır kapsamı %95,3. AOT/trim uyarısı sıfır.

## Gerçek veriyle neler öğrendim

Sana sormadan geçici bir hook kurup bu oturumun gerçek payload'larını yakaladım; hook'lar oturumu yeniden başlatmadan devreye girdi. Bulgular:
- `transcript_path` alanı senin kullanıcı adını içeriyor. Bu alanı kayda almıyorum.
- Hata veren komutlar sadece `PostToolUseFailure` üzerinden geliyor ve hata metni `"Exit code N"` biçiminde.
- Edit sonucunda `originalFile` ve `structuredPatch` alanları var. Diff, before/after hash'leri ve satır hash'leri doğrudan bunlardan çıkıyor.

Bu payload'lar temizlenip `fixtures/` altına kondu.

Bir de commit'ten önceki tarama, kod içinde senin Windows kısa kullanıcı adını (`HALILB~1`) yakaladı. Commit'ler henüz push edilmemişti; adı genel bir isimle değiştirip commit'leri yeniden oluşturdum, push edilen geçmişte o ad yok.
